test_title: PYST 65: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the correct reason as to why glucose and alcohol do NOT conduct electricity?

options.text: They do not form ions in solution.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They do not form ions in solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Electrical conductivity in a liquid medium depends entirely on the presence of mobile **charged particles**, specifically **ions** (cations and anions) or **free electrons**.
 
• **Glucose** (C₆H₁₂O₆) and **Alcohol** (such as **Ethanol**, C₂H₅OH) are categorized as **covalent compounds**. In these molecules, atoms are held together by the sharing of electrons rather than the transfer of electrons.
 
• When **Glucose** or **Alcohol** is dissolved in **water**, the molecules do not **dissociate** or break apart into ions; they remain as neutral, intact molecules throughout the solution.
 
• Because there is a total absence of **free ions** to carry the electric current between the positive and negative electrodes, these solutions act as **insulators**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The property of **evaporating quickly** (volatility) is related to intermolecular forces and vapor pressure, not to the ability to carry a charge in an aqueous state. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Substances that are **acidic in nature** (like **Hydrochloric acid**) conduct electricity because they release **Hydrogen ions (H+)** in water. Since **Glucose** and **Alcohol** do not release such ions, they are not acidic and do not conduct. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• These substances are organic molecules composed of **Carbon**, **Hydrogen**, and **Oxygen**, which are **non-metals**. They do not possess the metallic lattice or free electrons found in **metals**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolytes vs. Non-electrolytes:**
 
 
• **Electrolytes** are substances that produce ions when dissolved in a solvent (usually water) or when melted. Common examples include **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, **Sulfuric Acid (H₂SO₄)**, and **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**.
 
• **Non-electrolytes** are substances that do not provide ions in a solution. Examples include **Glucose**, **Urea**, and **Sucrose**. These solutions do not conduct **electricity**.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Ions:**
 
 
• In an electrolytic cell, the **anions** (negative ions) move toward the **anode** (+), and **cations** (positive ions) move toward the **cathode** (-). This movement of charges completes the electrical circuit.
 
• Without the formation of these ions, the flow of **electric current** through the liquid is physically impossible.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Bonding:**
 
 
• Most **organic compounds** involve **covalent bonding**. Unless these compounds have polar groups that can ionize (like the carboxyl group in **Acetic Acid**), they generally remain non-conductive.
 
• **Glucose** and **Alcohol** contain hydroxyl (-OH) groups, but unlike bases, these -OH groups are covalently bonded to carbon and do not dissociate as **hydroxide ions (OH-)** in water.
 
 
 
• **Distilled Water:**
 
 
• **Distilled water** itself is a very poor conductor of electricity because it is a covalent compound with negligible ionization. It only becomes conductive when **salts**, **acids**, or **bases** are added to provide the necessary ions.
 
 
</ul
